question: to the Commission Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE), Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová (Renew), Sandro Ruotolo (S&D), Krzysztof Brejza (PPE), Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Hilde Vautmans (Renew), Estelle Ceulemans (S&D), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Lynn Boylan (The Left), Sara Matthieu (Verts/ALE), Robert Biedroń (S&D), Thomas Waitz (Verts/ALE), Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew), Damien Carême (The Left), Sebastian Everding (The Left), Leila Chaibi (The Left), Hannah Neumann (Verts/ALE), Brando Benifei (S&D), Erik Marquardt (Verts/ALE), Markéta Gregorová (Verts/ALE), Birgit Sippel (S&D), Diana Riba i Giner (Verts/ALE), Barry Andrews (Renew), Nikolas Farantouris (S&D), Marco Tarquinio (S&D), Pernando Barrena Arza (The Left), Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Chloé Ridel (S&D) Subject:

The latest edition of ISS World Europe1, a trade fair on intelligence support systems for electronic surveillance, is taking place in Prague from 2 to 4 June 2026. The main sponsor of the event is NSO Group, developer of the Pegasus spyware, which has been used to unlawfully target journalists, activists, opposition politicians and others in several EU Member States. Among the other sponsors and exhibitors are companies linked to the unlawful use of surveillance technologies in various countries around the world. The fair is reportedly being attended by representatives of several EU governments. 1.
Will representatives of the Commission, or of any of its agencies or bodies, attend the ISS World Europe fair in June 2026?
Can the Commission confirm whether any such representatives have attended previous editions of ISS World Europe, and if so, in what capacity and with what outcome?

What internal guidelines, transparency requirements or safeguards govern participation by EU representatives in events involving companies active in the cyber-surveillance and dual-use technology sectors?
Supporter2
https://www.issworldtraining.com/iss_europe/sponsors.html. This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Cecilia Strada (S&D).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.9.2026) According to the Commission’s mission’s data, no representatives of the Commission, or its services attended the Intelligence Support Systems (ISS) World Europe Fair in June 2026 in Prague, or any previous editions of the ISS World Europe. The Commission assesses participation in external events on a case-by-case basis. Decisions are taken by the relevant Commission department considering the purpose of the event, the objectives of the participation, the expected contribution of Commission representatives, and the applicable administrative and budgetary rules. Commission officials are bound by the Staff Regulations1 and the applicable rules on ethics, integrity and conflicts of interest when participating in external events.
1 Council Regulation (EEC, Euratom, ECSC) No 259/68, OJ L 56, 4.3.1968, p. 1.
